old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-j2t9","title":"Rust egress gate lacks inner source/destination scope enforcement (C+Python deny, Rust egresses)","description":"Found by kimi-k3 security review of b7z9.93 (pass 2). Rust authorize_decapsulation (rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs:398-467) enforces NO unsafe/link-local/multicast address checks - scope is entirely delegated to caller-supplied booleans source_is_mesh/destination_is_mesh, and the production callers hardcode them: source_is_mesh: true at rust/lichen-gateway/src/resources.rs:1934 (authorize_egress) and destination_is_mesh: false at rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1429 (egress_tunnel_authorized). The is_local_mesh pre-check (gateway.rs:1410) covers link-local, GUA, NAT64 and routed 0200::/8 but lets multicast and ULA inner DESTINATIONS through as 'not mesh'. C enforces scope internally (tunnel_auth.c:475-478: unspecified/loopback/multicast/link-local source rejected via unsafe_addr + SOURCE_SCOPE; mesh-destination rejected via DESTINATION_SCOPE) and Python likewise (tunnel_auth.py:556-559). Consequence under the radio-adversary model: a mesh node holding ANY covering grant (the corpus itself accepts a /0 grant, accept_prefix_0) can egress a tunneled packet with inner source fe80::1/::1/multicast or inner destination ff02::1 through the Rust gateway where C and Python deny SOURCE_SCOPE/DESTINATION_SCOPE - weakened authorization plus a three-way data-path verdict divergence. Fix: move the scope checks inside Rust authorize_decapsulation (mirror C tunnel_auth.c unsafe_addr semantics exactly: reject unspecified/loopback/multicast/link-local inner source; reject multicast/unsafe/link-local/routable-02xx inner destination per the C code), keeping the booleans for the source_is_mesh prefix question or replacing them outright - mirror Python/C, update the wired tests, and consider a corpus decap case pinning link_local_source_rejected + multicast_destination for the Rust side too (they exist in the corpus already; only the Rust production path skips them). Do NOT weaken the vector runner's classification to compensate.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-10T03:42:48.541715257Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-09-10T03:42:48.541715257Z","labels":["security","gateway","networking"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-j2t9","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-b7z9.93","type":"discovered-from","created_at":"2026-09-10T03:42:48.667491722Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

new_value: Moved IPv6 scope enforcement inside Rust authorize_decapsulation, mirroring C tunnel_auth.c:443-478 exactly: new unsafe_addr (unspecified/loopback/ff00::/8) + is_link_local (fe80::/10) helpers; source denied on unsafe/link-local (SourceScope), destination denied on unsafe/link-local/first-byte-0x02 (DestinationScope), placed after grant selection + expiry eviction, before LRU touch (C/Python parity). DecapsulationRequest gained inner_destination; authorize_egress and gateway.rs egress_tunnel_authorized thread the real IPv6-header destination. Caller booleans kept (corpus classification unchanged - scoped corpus cases still resolve via booleans first). New unit test pins all 4 unsafe-source + 5 scoped-destination classes under a live /0 grant with production-hardcoded booleans. Tests: 9/9 tunnel_auth lib + 13/13 tunnel_auth_vectors pass; capability_announcements 2 failures confirmed pre-existing on HEAD (tracked by b8i2). 3x codereview via kimi-k3: correctness PASS, security PASS, edge-cases 1 fmt nit (new-line rustfmt drift) fixed inline pre-commit; file fmt drift back to pre-existing 12 hunks.
